rationale: Unspecified public SCF and stationary-force tiles resolve independently. Fitted restricted strict-FP64 gradient-dependent owners retain their hardware capability policy: eligible full-rate FP64 SCF owners use 1024 (nonlocal 512), and eligible all-electron through-d force owners on compute capability 8 or newer use 1024 for 48–128 atoms. Full-range device-fused strict-FP64 Direct RKS with zero application arithmetic budgets prefers 1024 on every supported CUDA device within the existing all-electron through-d, 48–128-atom, AO/grid-size and free-memory envelope, without a device profile or hardware allowlist. Explicit sizes, scientific controls, resource promises and bounded 256-point fallbacks remain authoritative. Historical endpoint evidence does not qualify new-source/device performance claims.
